items.title: Account Actions For Blackmaw Hold Abuse in WoW: Forever - November 17
items.summary: Account Actions For Blackmaw Hold Abuse in WoW: Forever - November 17 Originally Posted by Blizzard ( Blue Tracker / Official Forums ) As players continue their journey into WoW Forever’s higher-level content, we are closely monitoring the game economy to ensure that gold sources and costs are well balanced. Finding efficient farming spots has always been part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest. Over the past weekend, some players discovered a large group of non-elite enemies in the Blackmaw Hold dungeon that were incorrectly dropping the full amount of dungeon loot that would be expected from an elite. Early yesterday, we addressed this with a hotfix, and since then, we have been investigating the overall economic impact. Players who simply ran Blackmaw Hold a few times and benefited organically from the extra loot did nothing wrong, and no one should worry that they’re putting their account at risk if they accidentally benefit from a bug. But there were a couple hundred players worldwide who recognized that this was unintended and spent significant time exclusively farming that group of enemies. When : 17 November–8 December Where : Caverns of Time in Tanaris Grab the quest from any Holiday Celebrants and hitch a ride to the Caverns of Time through portals located in Orgrimmar and Stormwind. Players receive an automatic 10% Experience and Reputation buff during the Anniversary Event. They must complete the repeatable Celebrate Good Fun! quest from Yllana in Tanaris every day to add another 10% to the total . The anniversary event buff also stacks with other XP and Reputation buffs. +20% XP and Reputation from the Anniversary Event. +25% XP buff from the Five Warband Mentors: Midnight achievement. +15% XP and Gold from War Mode. +10% from the Draught of Ten Lands potion. This works for characters level 49 and lower . items.title: Player-Level Dungeon XP Adjustment - November 14
items.summary: Player-Level Dungeon XP Adjustment - November 14 Originally Posted by Blizzard ( Blue Tracker / Official Forums ) Yesterday, we updated dungeon play so that experience granted by an enemy in an instance is nullified if a high level player is in the group and enemy is trivial to that player. For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon. With hotfixes that are now live, we’ve just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so that the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies. Please note that this adjustment will not apply in instances that were already underway when it was deployed (a few minutes ago). Thank you very much!

items.title: Raid Encounter Design in Midnight Season 3
items.summary: Raid Encounter Design in Midnight Season 3 Originally Posted by Blizzard ( Blue Tracker / Official Forums ) Last week we made several adjustments to The Venomous Abyss with the intent of reducing the number of damage events that could kill you or your entire raid with a single individual mistake. We believe this type of severe mechanical penalty was used too often in The Venomous Abyss, causing the associated mechanics to become frustrating as the season wore on. Our goal with these changes was to ensure that damage events feel more proportional to player mistakes and to reduce the number of instances where individual mistakes could easily trigger group wipes. A couple examples from that list of changes: Malice damage was reduced by 45% on Mythic and 63% on Normal/Heroic, which should now help a failed interrupt feel like a punishing but recoverable group mistake. Reductions to Noxious Splash’s initial damage (33%) and damage-over-time component (84%) should help ensure that a single individual’s mistake no longer feels like a death sentence. We feel that our design has shifted over time at the expense of the average Mythic player’s experience. Going forward into Season 3, we’d like to intentionally pull back on some of these severe mechanical penalties, even at the start of the season.
